specification.problem: Approximate combinatorial optimization (MaxCut on regular graphs) with a depth-p parameterized quantum circuit built from gates whose locality is at most that of the objective function. This is the QAOA setting.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction: p=1 circuit for MaxCut on a tiny explicit instance (assumed 3-vertex triangle... to keep it simple, 4-vertex cycle C4, 2-regular). Only the standard QAOA ansatz and the objective are given. Outside scope: the 0.6924 ratio derivation for 3-regular graphs, general-p analysis, classical parameter preprocessing, the strategy for p growing with input size, and the 2-regular analysis.

symbols.domain: positive integer; n=4 in the assumed instance

symbols.meaning: MaxCut objective, the number of cut edges
mixer operator, sum of Pauli X

equations.label: MaxCut objective
equations.description: Cut size as a sum of 2-local clauses, one per edge.
equations.justification: Standard MaxCut definition; the abstract only names MaxCut and says gate locality is at most that of the objective.

equations.label: Phase and mixer operators
equations.latex: U(C,\gamma)=e^{-i\gamma C}=\prod_{(j,k)\in E}e^{-i\gamma C_{jk}},\quad U(B,\beta)=e^{-i\beta B}=\prod_{j=1}^n e^{-i\beta X_j}
equations.description: Layer unitaries. Each factor acts on at most the locality of the objective clauses (2 qubits for MaxCut), consistent with the abstract's locality claim.
equations.justification: Standard QAOA construction recalled from background. The abstract does not state these forms or the exact gate set.
assumptions: The paper's algorithm is the standard QAOA ansatz

equations.label: Depth-p state
equations.abstract_quote: The algorithm depends on an integer $p\geq 1$
equations.justification: The abstract says the algorithm depends on p and the circuit depth grows linearly in p times the number of constraints, which is consistent with p repeated layers of clause-wise gates. The exact ansatz is background.
assumptions: Initial state is the uniform superposition

equations.label: Expected objective
equations.description: Quantity to optimize classically over angles.
equations.justification: Standard QAOA objective. The abstract mentions classical preprocessing for fixed p, which is presumably angle selection, but this is not stated.

equations.label: Approximation guarantee form
equations.description: The quoted guarantee, applying to the cut found by the algorithm.
equations.abstract_quote: For $p=1$, on 3-regular graphs the quantum algorithm always finds a cut that is at least 0.6924 times the size of the optimal cut.
equations.justification: Directly stated in the abstract; the derivation is not reconstructed.

registers.name: q
registers.size: n (assumed n=4 for the C4 instance)
registers.role: one qubit per vertex; bit z_j encodes the side of the cut for vertex j, with qubit j labelled by vertex j

steps.description: Prepare the uniform superposition on all qubits using Hadamard gates.
For layer k=1..p apply the phase operator, i.e. a two-qubit ZZ-rotation for each edge with angle gamma_k, then the mixer, i.e. a single-qubit X-rotation per qubit with angle beta_k.
Choose angles by classical optimization of the expected cut (assumed form of the classical preprocessing).

specification.measurement: Measure all qubits in the computational basis and keep the best cut found over repeated shots (assumed).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Evaluate C(z) classically for each sampled bitstring and return the largest. Angle optimization is as in eq_4 (assumed).
assumptions: Algorithm taken to be the standard QAOA ansatz; the abstract does not give the explicit circuit.
Tiny instance chosen: p=1 on the 4-cycle C4 (2-regular) as an illustration.
The abstract's strategy for p growing with input size and its preprocessing details are not reconstructed.
